 Advertisement Lee County school district considers closing two schools amid budget cuts
 Advertisement Updated: 7:20 PM EST Nov 12, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Dave Elias Reporter Derrick Shaw Digital Content Manager Lee County school district considers closing two schools amid budget cuts
 Updated: 7:20 PM EST Nov 12, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Dave Elias Reporter Derrick Shaw Digital Content Manager FORT MYERS, Fla. — The Lee County School District is proposing the closure of Tice Elementary and Orangewood Elementary , citing budget cuts and a decline of more than 2,000 students over the past few years.
 "When we see a decline in our students to the tune of more than 2,000 students in a short period of time over the last couple of years, we have conversations to include closure of schools," said Superintendent Dr. Denise Carlin. 
 Advertisement Tice Elementary, one of the district’s oldest schools, is slated to close after 100 years of operation. Combined, the closures would impact approximately 1,000 students from Title I schools, which receive federal funding. 
 "Where will the children go? We do have other schools that have some capacity. We'll try very hard to help parents get into the school they would like to," Carlin said. 
 District maps show nearby schools as potential options for students from Tice and Orangewood. The two schools, which primarily serve low-income families, employ more than 60 teachers. 
 "We want to make sure to the extent we can that there is a place for our teachers and our support staff," Carlin said. 
 Carlin explained that as students transition to other schools, teachers will still be needed, though she anticipates some will choose to retire or transfer. 
 "People do choose to leave. They choose to retire. We still have people who transfer," she added. 
 The closures are expected to save the district $40 million over seven years. "Quite frankly, where these two schools are located, that is not where young families are choosing to be," Carlin said. 
 She also noted that the district is slated to open four new schools in the Lehigh Acres area within the next two years. The proposal will be presented at the next Lee County school board meeting for a vote.
